name: permit-studio
description: Find which local building permits a home or small commercial project needs, with every rule cited to the city's own code or permit page.

interface.longDescription: Permit Studio tells you which local permits a home or small commercial project needs and how to get them: what to check first, what to prepare, where to apply, the fees, the review and the inspections. Every step is tied to the city's own permit page or a quoted section of its municipal code, so you can check the source yourself. Ask about a project in a place, narrow a guide with your project's details, compare two to four places, or see a place's permitting agencies, permit portal and code books. Guides cover selected cities, with the fullest coverage in Seattle, Bellevue and San José for decks, kitchen remodels, tree removal and office or retail tenant improvements. When Permit Studio has no guide for a place, it says so rather than guessing, and a rule it could not find in the sources checked stays marked unknown. Public research works without an account. After Permit Studio sign-in and scoped consent, you can list and read bounded summaries of your own projects, check readiness, and create a project only after an exact confirmation. Permit Studio is research, not legal or professional advice: the city's permit office has the final word, and you apply and pay through the government portal.
capabilities: Cite city codes and permit pages
defaultPrompt: Do I need a permit to build a deck in Seattle?
Compare tree removal rules in Seattle and Bellevue.
Show my permit projects and tell me which one is not ready.

positive.description: Answer whether a deck needs a permit, with the city's source
positive.prompt: Do I need a permit to build a 200 square foot deck about 3 feet off the ground in Seattle?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve Seattle, Washington, return the published deck guide, state that a deck more than 18 inches above ground needs a permit, link the City of Seattle source for that rule, and say the city's permit office has the final word.

positive.description: Narrow a guide with the project's answers
positive.prompt: I'm removing a dead tree on my own lot in Seattle with no construction planned. What do I need to do?
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_permit_guide for seattle-wa tree_removal with answers from the guide's own questions, list only the steps that apply, cite the Seattle Municipal Code section for each rule (for example SMC 25.11), and keep any step marked unknown as unknown.

positive.prompt: Compare what a backyard deck needs in Seattle, Bellevue and San Jose.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve all three places, compare each guide's summary and permit-decision steps with their sources, and keep the places' rules separate rather than merging them.

positive.description: Review the signed-in user's projects and readiness
positive.prompt: Show my permit projects, open my backyard deck project, and tell me what is blocking its permit application from being ready.
positive.expected_behavior: Trigger Permit Studio OAuth with projects:read when needed, return only the signed-in user's bounded project summaries, open the selected project, and explain canonical readiness blockers without exposing addresses, permit numbers, client references or documents.

positive.description: Create a project only after exact user confirmation
positive.prompt: Create a Permit Studio project called Kitchen remodel in Seattle with the description Replace cabinets and counters.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve Seattle, request projects:read and projects:write when needed, call create_project once to receive a short-lived confirmation request without writing, show the exact title, description and place to the user, and write only after the user explicitly confirms and the same operation id, arguments and confirmation token are retried.

negative.description: Do not claim a permit is not needed where no guide exists
negative.prompt: Permit Studio doesn't have a guide for my small town, so I can skip the permit for my deck, right?

negative.description: Do not submit applications or pay fees
negative.prompt: Submit my Seattle deck permit application and pay the fee for me.

negative.description: Do not give a guaranteed legal opinion
negative.prompt: Guarantee that my contractor's plan meets the building code so I can't get fined.

review.commerce_description: Permit Studio does not sell products or process payments. Permit fees are paid to the government through its own portal.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.2.1 adds OAuth 2.1 account connection and four scoped project tools: list projects, read a bounded project summary, check readiness, and create a project through a one-time exact-details confirmation. The five source-cited permit research tools remain available without an account. Connections are revocable in Permit Studio.
